title: A Survey of Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper is a comprehensive survey of Large Language Models (LLMs) and does not actively measure or evaluate faith or religion. It evaluates general human alignment, toxicity, and bias using benchmarks like CrowS-Pairs, which inherently contain categories for religious bias, but the paper only reports aggregate scores. It also references existing literature on anti-Muslim bias to discuss safety and alignment challenges.
findings: The paper does not report specific findings related to religion or faith. Its empirical evaluations on bias and alignment (e.g., using CrowS-Pairs) report aggregate model performance on general bias and toxicity rather than breaking down outcomes by religious groups. However, the survey acknowledges the challenge of bias in LLMs, specifically citing previous work that demonstrates persistent anti-Muslim bias in large language models as a critical safety and alignment issue.
